title: Minnesota Man Pleads Guilty to Attempting to Support ISIS, Praised New Orleans Attack - NewsBreak
text:
4 hours ago MINNEAPOLIS – A 23-year-old Minnesota man pleaded guilty Wednesday to attempting to provide material support and resources to a foreign terrorist organization, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Minnesota.
Photo by Tingey Injury Law Firm on Unsplash Abdisatar Ahmed Hassan admitted to attempting to join ISIS after twice trying to travel from Minnesota to Somalia in December 2024. Prosecutors said FBI agents tracked both efforts, which included surveillance at airports in Minnesota and Chicago. During his second attempt, Customs and Border Protection agents intercepted him in Chicago and found personal documents in his only carry-on bag.
“There is no margin for error when it comes to terrorism,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Joseph H. Thompson. “Hassan flew the ISIS flag, venerated attacks on the homeland, and wanted to kill Americans. We are not taking chances. We will not let Minnesota become a safe haven for terrorists.”
Court records revealed that Hassan used social media to promote propaganda videos calling for jihad in Somalia and praised ISIS-inspired attacks, including a New Orleans massacre on January 1, 2025, that killed 14 people. The day after that attack, he described the assailant as “the legend that killed Americans.”
The FBI said Hassan communicated directly with an ISIS recruiter, downloaded sniper training manuals, and posted videos of himself displaying knives and a homemade ISIS flag. When he was arrested in February 2025, agents seized two cellphones, the knife, and the flag.
“Today’s guilty plea reflects many hours of hard work by agents and analysts from the FBI,” said FBI Minneapolis Special Agent in Charge Alvin M. Winston Sr. “Keeping Minnesota safe from those who support Designated Foreign Terrorist Organizations like ISIS and Al Shabab is a top priority of the FBI.”
Hassan entered his plea before U.S. District Judge Donovan W. Frank. He remains in custody while awaiting sentencing.
